# Target Selection

```{r, warning = FALSE, message=FALSE}
target <- "HRFS12MD"
```

# Research Question

The goal of this analysis is to develop a predictive model of how food insecure an individual is in the US based on various factors collected through the Current Population Survey. By understanding factors that contribute to food insecurity and being able to predict who is most at risk, steps can be taken to create interventions that target specific factors or populations. The issue of food insecurity in the US is particularly relevant right now, because the USDA recently announced it has cancelled the release of their Household Food Security Reports, essentially putting an end to this dataset for the time being. For this reason, utilizing this dataset is also an opportunity to highlight the value this survey data can provide, particularly as a way to inform policy decisions and interventions that far offset any "cost" related to the data's collection.

Because the target selected is an ordinal variable, logistic regression will be used to predict whether an individual is food secure (0) or considered food insecure to some extent (1). Further analysis may better reflect what variables lead to higher food insecurity, but these models will focus on understanding what variables are associated with food insecurity in general.

# Feature Selection

```{r}
features <- c(
  "HRNUMHOU", # total number of persons living in household
  "PRNMCHLD", # number of children ind. has
  "GEDIV", # division/region of the US they live in
  "GTMETSTA", # whether their city is metropolitan or not
  "PESEX", # ind.'s sex
  "PRTAGE", # ind.'s age
  "PEMARITL", # ind.'s marital status
  "PEEDUCA", # highest level of school completed
  "PTDTRACE", # ind.'s race
  "PRCITSHP", # citizenship status
  "PEMLR", # employment status
  "PEHRUSLT", # hours worked per week
  "PRMJOCC1", # field/type of employment
  "PESCHENR", # currently enrolled in school or not
  "HEFAMINC", # family income
  "HETENURE" # whether residence is owned/rented
)
```

# Feature Encoding

```{r, warning = FALSE, message=FALSE}
str(data_final)
```

Handle missing predictor data

```{r, warning = FALSE, message=FALSE}
# drop 'hours vary' for hours worked BEFORE replacing with NA
data_final <- data_final %>%
  filter(!(PEHRUSLT %in% c(-4))) 

# define the NA codes using in this dataset
na_codes <- c(-9, -1, "NA")

# replace with NA
data_final <- naniar::replace_with_na_all(
  data_final, condition = ~.x %in% na_codes
)

data_sample <- data_final %>% slice_sample(n = 5000)  

# visualize some missing data
naniar::vis_miss(data_sample) # overall
naniar::gg_miss_upset(data_sample) # across diff variables
naniar::gg_miss_fct(x = data_sample, fct = HRFS12MD) # across food security
```

All variables are already numeric, but some are categorical, so encode as factors.

```{r, warning = FALSE, message=FALSE}
# encode categorical
con_vars <- c("HRNUMHOU", "PRNMCHLD", "PRTAGE", "PEHRUSLT")

cat_vars <- c(
  "HRFS12MD",  # food security (target) --> drop
  "GEDIV",     # division/region --> drop
  "GTMETSTA",  # metro status --> drop
  "PESEX",     # sex --> drop
  "PEMARITL",  # marital status --> underage and thus unmarried
  "PEEDUCA",   # education --> underage / not applicable
  "PTDTRACE",  # race --> drop
  "PRCITSHP",  # citizenship --> unknown
  "PEMLR",     # labor force status --> underage / not applicable
  "PRMJOCC1",  # occupation --> na = unemployed
  "PESCHENR",  # school enrollment --> no
  "HEFAMINC", # family income --> no missing, imputed by surveyors
  "HETENURE"   # housing tenure --> inpute w/ ??
)

# recode and replace as necessary
data_final <- data_final %>%
  mutate(
    PEMARITL = fct_explicit_na(as_factor(PEMARITL), na_level = "6"),   # missing -> never married
    PEEDUCA = fct_explicit_na(as_factor(PEEDUCA), na_level = "Unknown"),
    PTDTRACE = fct_collapse(as_factor(PTDTRACE),
                             "Other Mixed Race" = c(11, 12,13,14,17,18,19,20,22,23,24,25,26)),
    PRCITSHP = fct_explicit_na(as_factor(PRCITSHP), na_level = "Unknown"),
    PEMLR = fct_explicit_na(as_factor(PEMLR), na_level = "8"),
    PRMJOCC1 = fct_explicit_na(as_factor(PRMJOCC1), na_level = "12"),
    PESCHENR = fct_explicit_na(as_factor(PESCHENR), na_level = "2"),
    HETENURE = fct_explicit_na(as_factor(HETENURE), na_level = "Unknown")
  )

# lastly, make target dichotomous
data_final <- data_final %>%
  mutate(
    HRFS12MD = case_when(
      HRFS12MD == 1 ~ 0,           # no food insecurity
      HRFS12MD %in% 2:4 ~ 1,       # some food insecurity
      TRUE ~ NA_real_               # everything else -> NA
    ),
    HRFS12MD = factor(HRFS12MD)    # convert to factor for modeling
  )

# finalize data
data_final <- data_final %>%
  mutate(
    across(all_of(cat_vars), forcats::as_factor),
    across(all_of(con_vars), as.numeric),
    )

data_hold <- data_final
```

# Data Splitting

First, we remove any rows of data where food security status is missing. These consist of participants who were not asked that segment of the survey (-1) and those who did not respond (-9).

Then, data is split into `data_test` and `data_train`, keeping equivalent proportions of the target variable in the testing and training sets. 70% of the data will be used in the training set, while the remaining 30% will be allocated to the test set.

```{r, warning = FALSE, message=FALSE}
data_final <- data_final[!is.na(data_final$HRFS12MD),]

#ensure factor levels are named properly
data_final <- data_final %>%
  mutate(across(where(is.factor), ~{
    f <- factor(.x)
    levels(f) <- make.names(levels(f))
    f
  }))

split <- initial_split(data_final[!is.na(data_final[, target]), ], prop = 0.7, strata = target)

data_train <- training(split)
data_test <- testing(split)
```

# Define the recipe

Defines a recipe where you impute missing numeric data, encode factor predictors as dummy variables, and scale and center all numeric variables.

```{r, warning = FALSE, message=FALSE}

blueprint <- recipe(HRFS12MD ~ ., data = data_train) %>%
  step_impute_bag(all_predictors()) %>%
  step_dummy(all_factor_predictors(), one_hot = FALSE) %>%
  step_center(all_numeric(), -all_outcomes()) %>%
  step_scale(all_numeric(), -all_outcomes())

blueprint
```

# Fit the Models

We will be fitting three models:

1.  Model using lasso
2.  Model using ridge
3.  Model using elastic net

```{r, warning = FALSE, message=FALSE}
set.seed(123)  # for reproducibility

# Cross-validation control
ctrl <- trainControl(
  method = "cv",
  number = 10,
  classProbs = TRUE,
  summaryFunction = twoClassSummary
)

# Model 1: Lasso
lasso_grid <- expand.grid(
  alpha = 1,
  lambda = 10^seq(-3, 1, length.out = 100)
)

model_lasso <- train(
  blueprint, 
  data = data_train, 
  method = "glmnet",
  preProc = c("zv", "center", "scale"),
  metric = "ROC",
  trControl = ctrl,
  tuneGrid = lasso_grid
)

# Model 2: Ridge
ridge_grid <- expand.grid(
  alpha = 0, 
  lambda = 10^seq(-3, 1, length.out = 100)
)

model_ridge <- train(
  blueprint, 
  data = data_train, 
  method = "glmnet",
  preProc = c("zv", "center", "scale"),
  metric = "ROC",
  trControl = ctrl,
  tuneGrid = ridge_grid
)

# Model 3: Elastic Net
elastic_grid <- expand.grid(
  alpha = 0.5, 
  lambda = 10^seq(-3, 1, length.out = 100)
)

model_elastic <- train(
  blueprint, 
  data = data_train, 
  method = "glmnet",
  preProc = c("zv", "center", "scale"),
  metric = "ROC",
  trControl = ctrl,
  tuneGrid = elastic_grid
)
```

# Examine Performance

Examine the performance for the three models.

```{r, warning = FALSE, message=FALSE}
rsamples <- resamples(list(
  Lasso = model_lasso, 
  Ridge = model_ridge, 
  ElasticNet = model_elastic
))

summary(rsamples)

bwplot(rsamples, metric = "ROC")
```

# Key Coefficients

```{r}
# --- LASSO COEFFICIENTS ---
best_lambda_lasso <- model_lasso$bestTune$lambda
coef_lasso <- coef(model_lasso$finalModel, s = best_lambda_lasso)

coef_lasso_df <- data.frame(
  variable = rownames(as.matrix(coef_lasso)),
  coefficient = as.numeric(coef_lasso)
)
coef_lasso_df <- coef_lasso_df[order(abs(coef_lasso_df$coefficient), decreasing = TRUE), ]
head(coef_lasso_df, 10)


# --- RIDGE COEFFICIENTS ---
best_lambda_ridge <- model_ridge$bestTune$lambda
coef_ridge <- coef(model_ridge$finalModel, s = best_lambda_ridge)

coef_ridge_df <- data.frame(
  variable = rownames(as.matrix(coef_ridge)),
  coefficient = as.numeric(coef_ridge)
)
coef_ridge_df <- coef_ridge_df[order(abs(coef_ridge_df$coefficient), decreasing = TRUE), ]
head(coef_ridge_df, 10)


# --- ELASTIC NET COEFFICIENTS ---
best_lambda_elastic <- model_elastic$bestTune$lambda
coef_elastic <- coef(model_elastic$finalModel, s = best_lambda_elastic)

coef_elastic_df <- data.frame(
  variable = rownames(as.matrix(coef_elastic)),
  coefficient = as.numeric(coef_elastic)
)
coef_elastic_df <- coef_elastic_df[order(abs(coef_elastic_df$coefficient), decreasing = TRUE), ]
head(coef_elastic_df, 10)
```

# View Important Predictors

```{r}
library(vip)

vip(model_elastic, num_features = 16, method = "model")
vip(model_lasso, num_features = 16, method = "model")
vip(model_ridge, num_features = 16, method = "model")
```

I selected elastic net as the final model because it balanced both sensitivity and specificity without

```{r}
pred_class <- predict(model_elastic, newdata = data_test)

confusionMatrix(
  data = relevel(pred_class, ref = "X0"),
  reference = relevel(as.factor(data_test[[target]]), ref = "X0")
)
```
